working_dir.description: Working directory for command execution. Supports tilde expansion (e.g., ~/projects). If not specified, uses the current working directory.

summary.description: A brief explanation of what the command does

toolSpecification.name: execute_bash
toolSpecification.description: Execute the specified bash command. NEVER prefix commands with cd to change the working directory, use the `working_dir` argument instead.

summary.description: Optional description of the purpose of this batch operation (mainly useful for multiple operations)

operations.description: Array of operations to execute. Provide one element for single operation, multiple for batch.

start_line.description: Starting line number (optional, for Line mode). A negative index represents a line number starting from the end of the file.

mode.description: The operation mode to run in: `Line`, `Directory`, `Search`. `Line` and `Search` are only for text files, and `Directory` is only for directories. `Image` is for image files, in this mode `image_paths` is required.

pattern.description: Pattern to search for (required, for Search mode). Case insensitive. The pattern matching is performed per line.

context_lines.description: Number of context lines around search results (optional, for Search mode)

depth.description: Depth of a recursive directory listing (optional, for Directory mode)

exclude_patterns.description: Glob patterns to exclude from directory listing (optional, for Directory mode). If omitted, uses defaults. If empty array [] is provided, no exclusions are applied (shows everything). If patterns are provided, they completely override the defaults. Examples: '**/target/**', '*.log'

end_line.description: Ending line number (optional, for Line mode). A negative index represents a line number starting from the end of the file.

max_entries.description: Maximum number of entries to return (optional, for Directory mode). When limit is reached, results are truncated and metadata shows 'showing X of Y entries'. Use to prevent context window overflow. Default: 1000

image_paths.description: List of paths to the images. This is currently supported by the Image mode.

offset.description: Number of entries to skip for pagination (optional, for Directory mode). Use with max_entries to iterate through large directories. Entries are sorted by last modified time (most recent first). Default: 0

path.description: Path to the file or directory. The path should be absolute, or otherwise start with ~ for the user's home (required for Line, Directory, Search modes).

toolSpecification.name: fs_read
toolSpecification.description:
Tool for reading files, directories and images. Always provide an 'operations' array.

For single operation: provide array with one element.
For batch operations: provide array with multiple elements.

Available modes:
- Line: Read lines from a file
- Directory: List directory contents
- Search: Search for patterns in files
- Image: Read and process images

Examples:
1. Single: {"operations": [{"mode": "Line", "path": "/file.txt"}]}
2. Batch: {"operations": [{"mode": "Line", "path": "/file1.txt"}, {"mode": "Search", "path": "/file2.txt", "pattern": "test"}]}

file_text.description: Required parameter of `create` command, with the content of the file to be created.

old_str.description: Required parameter of `str_replace` command containing the string in `path` to replace.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. `/repo/file.py` or `/repo`.

summary.description: A brief explanation of what the file change does or why it's being made.

insert_line.description: Required parameter of `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line `insert_line` of `path`.

new_str.description: Required parameter of `str_replace` command containing the new string. Required parameter of `insert` command containing the string to insert. Required parameter of `append` command containing the content to append to the file.

command.description: The commands to run. Allowed options are: `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `append`.

toolSpecification.name: fs_write
toolSpecification.description:
A tool for creating and editing files
 * The `create` command will override the file at `path` if it already exists as a file, and otherwise create a new file
 * The `append` command will add content to the end of an existing file, automatically adding a newline if the file doesn't end with one. The file must exist.
 Notes for using the `str_replace` command:
 * The `old_str` parameter should match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the original file. Be mindful of whitespaces!
 * If the `old_str` parameter is not unique in the file, the replacement will not be performed. Make sure to include enough context in `old_str` to make it unique
 * The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that should replace the `old_str`.

limit.description: Maximum files to return. If totalFiles exceeds this, truncated will be true.

path.description: Root directory to search from. Only set this when the user explicitly mentions a directory path. In all other cases, omit this so the tool searches from the current working directory (the project root).

max_depth.description: Maximum directory depth to traverse. Increase for deep nested structures.

toolSpecification.name: glob
toolSpecification.description: Find files and directories whose paths match a glob pattern. Respects .gitignore. Prefer this over the bash 'find' command for listing or discovering paths. Returns JSON with totalFiles (count found), truncated (true if limited), and filePaths array. When truncated is true, just mention results are truncated, don't state the limit number.

path.description: Directory to search from. Defaults to current working directory.

max_matches_per_file.description: Max matches returned per file (output limit). Increase to see all occurrences in a file.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to search for. Examples: 'fn main', 'class.*Component', 'TODO|FIXME'. Start with simple patterns first (e.g. just the word you're looking for), then refine if needed.

max_files.description: Max number of files returned (output limit). Increase for comprehensive codebase searches.

output_mode.description: Output format: 'content' returns matches as 'file:line:content' (default, best for seeing actual matches), 'files_with_matches' returns only file paths, 'count' returns match counts per file.

max_depth.description: Max directory depth to traverse when searching (search limit). Increase for deeply nested structures.

max_total_lines.description: Max total matched lines returned across all files (output limit). Increase when searching for many occurrences.

toolSpecification.name: grep
toolSpecification.description:
Fast text pattern search in files using regex. ALWAYS use this tool instead of 'grep', 'rg', or 'ag' commands in bash. Respects .gitignore.

## Text Discovery Only
Use grep for literal text/pattern matching: error messages, TODOs, config values, regex patterns.

## For Semantic Code Understanding → Use 'code' tool if available
- Finding symbol definitions or usages → code tool (search_symbols, goto_definition, find_references)
- Understanding code structure/relationships → code tool
- Distinguishing definition vs call vs import → code tool

## Fallback
If the 'code' tool is available but returns insufficient symbol info, use grep to discover candidate files/lines, then return to 'code' for precise navigation.

When you use this tool, prefer to show the user a small list of representative matches (including file paths and line numbers) instead of only giving a high-level summary.

command.description: The commands to run. Allowed options are `ListAgents` to query available agents, or `InvokeSubagents` to invoke one or more subagents

query.description: The query or task to be handled by the subagent

relevant_context.description: Optional additional context that should be provided to the subagent to help it understand the task better

agent_name.description: Optional name of the specific agent to use. If not provided, uses the default agent

subagents.description: Array of subagent invocations to execute in parallel. Each invocation specifies a query, optional agent name, and optional context.

content.description: Required for `InvokeSubagents` command. Contains subagents array and optional conversation ID.

toolSpecification.name: use_subagent
toolSpecification.description:
⚠️ CRITICAL DELEGATION TOOL ⚠️

🔍 BEFORE attempting ANY task, CHECK if you have the required tools in YOUR current tool list.

❌ If you DON'T have the necessary tools → YOU MUST use this tool to delegate to a subagent that does.
✅ If you DO have the tools → Handle the task yourself.

## When to Use (MANDATORY scenarios):

1. **MISSING TOOLS**: The user asks you to do something but you don't see the required tool in your available tools list
   - Example: User asks to read a file, but you don't have 'fs_read' → USE THIS TOOL
   - Example: User asks to search code, but you don't have 'code' tool → USE THIS TOOL
   - Example: User asks to run bash command, but you don't have 'execute_bash' → USE THIS TOOL

2. **PARALLEL PROCESSING**: A complex task can be split into independent subtasks that different specialized agents can handle simultaneously

3. **CAPABILITY CHECK**: Use ListAgents command first to see what specialized agents and their toolsets are available

## @prompt References in Queries

You CAN pass `@prompt-name` references (including arguments) directly in the subagent query field. The system automatically resolves @prompt references before the subagent starts — the prompt content is expanded inline and the subagent receives the fully resolved text. Do NOT refuse to delegate because a query contains `@prompt-name` syntax.

Example: `{"query": "@my-task 'arg1:value1, arg2:value2'"}` — this is valid and will be resolved.

## How Subagents Are Different:
- Subagents have DIFFERENT, SPECIALIZED toolsets than you
- Each subagent may have tools you don't have access to
- They operate independently with their own context
- Up to 4 subagents can work in parallel

## Decision Flow:
```
User makes request → Check YOUR tools list → Missing required tool? → USE use_subagent
                                          → Have required tool? → Handle it yourself
```

⚡ Remember: Don't apologize about lacking tools - just delegate to a subagent that has them! Also note that subagents that are spawned together could not communicate with each other. If they are to perform tasks that are dependent on each other. Spawn them with a different tool call!

toolSpecification.name: browser_navigate
toolSpecification.description: Navigate the headless Chromium browser to a URL. Page state persists across calls. Returns the final URL, HTTP status, and page title.

wait_until.description: When to consider navigation done. Default: domcontentloaded.

toolSpecification.name: browser_text
toolSpecification.description: Get the visible text content (document.body.innerText) of the currently loaded page. Use this to read what's on the page after navigating.

toolSpecification.name: browser_eval
toolSpecification.description: Evaluate a JavaScript expression in the page context. Useful for reading DOM (e.g. document.querySelector('h1').innerText) or extracting structured data. Expression is wrapped in an async IIFE so you can use await. Return value must be JSON-serializable.

toolSpecification.name: browser_click
toolSpecification.description: Click an element matching the given CSS selector. Waits up to 15s for the element to appear.

toolSpecification.name: browser_type
toolSpecification.description: Fill an input/textarea matching the selector with the given text (replaces existing value).

selector.description: CSS selector for the input element.

toolSpecification.name: browser_screenshot
toolSpecification.description: Take a PNG screenshot of the current viewport and save it to the workspace. Returns the saved path. Use this when you need to show the user what the page looks like.

path.description: Output path inside workspace, e.g. '/workspace/shot.png'. Default: /workspace/screenshot.png

name.description: Skill name (matches the 'name' field in the skill file's frontmatter).

toolSpecification.name: load_skill
toolSpecification.description: Load the full body of a named skill (a reusable playbook). Use BEFORE acting on a task that matches one of the available skills' descriptions. Returns the markdown content of the skill.

toolSpecification.name: verify_change
toolSpecification.description: Validate edits. Use AFTER fs_write or shell edits, and BEFORE telling the user 'done'. Runs: py_compile of given files; HTTP GET of given URLs (expect <400); checks 'absent_in' patterns (must NOT appear), 'present_in' patterns (must appear), and 'shell' commands (must exit 0). Returns header 'VERIFY=OK' or 'VERIFY=FAIL' and per-check lines. If FAIL — fix and re-run.

py_files.description: Absolute paths to python files to byte-compile.

absent_in.description: Patterns that must NOT appear in given files (catches broken refs).

toolSpecification.name: plan
toolSpecification.description: Maintain a structured TODO list for the current task. ALWAYS call `plan` with op=set at the start of any multi-step request (≥2 actions). Update items as you progress (`op=update` with status=in_progress / done / skipped). Statuses: pending, in_progress, done, skipped. The user sees the list in the UI. Operations: set (replace all items), update (change one item by index), add (append, optionally after index), clear (empty).

items.description: For op=set: list of step descriptions (strings) or {text,status} objects.

after.description: For op=add: insert after this index.

toolSpecification.name: change_dir
toolSpecification.description: Change the persistent working directory for this session. Subsequent execute_bash, patch, fs_* calls use it by default. Relative paths are resolved against the current cwd. Returns the new absolute cwd.

toolSpecification.name: patch
toolSpecification.description: Multi-operation file editor with named clipboards. Use INSTEAD of fs_write when: (a) you need several edits in one shot, (b) you want to move/copy code via clipboards (use toClipboard on the source, fromClipboard at the destination), or (c) you need to change indentation while moving (reindent: {strip, add}). Operations per patch: 'replace' (oldText must be unique), 'append_eof', 'prepend_bof', 'overwrite' (replaces whole file). Auto-creates .bak.<ts>. Clipboards persist across patch calls in the same session.

toClipboard.description: Save oldText under this clipboard name before the edit.

fromClipboard.description: Use clipboard content as newText (overrides newText).

strip.description: Prefix to remove from each line of newText.

add.description: Prefix to add to each line of newText after stripping.

toolSpecification.name: llm_one_shot
toolSpecification.description: Single-turn LLM call with NO history and NO tools. Use for: summarization, classification, extraction, reformatting, rewriting. Cheaper than spawning a subagent. Default model is claude-haiku-4.5 to keep costs down. Returns the model's full text response.

model.description: Model id (e.g. claude-haiku-4.5, claude-sonnet-4.6). Defaults to haiku.

max_tokens.description: Soft cap on response length (truncated post-hoc).

toolSpecification.name: output_iframe
toolSpecification.description: Render an HTML snippet for the user as a sandboxed iframe in the chat. Use to show: charts (Vega-Lite via CDN), SVG diagrams, HTML/CSS demos, interactive widgets. The HTML must be self-contained; external resources via https CDN only. Do NOT use for plain text — write a normal reply instead.

toolSpecification.name: keyword_search
toolSpecification.description: Locate the most relevant files for a multi-term query, ranked by score. Use INSTEAD of grep when navigating an unfamiliar codebase with vague intent. Heuristics: matches in definition lines (def/class/function) score higher; matches in filenames score higher; files hitting more distinct terms rank higher. Provide MANY SPECIFIC terms ordered by importance.

search_terms.description: Terms in descending order of importance.

toolSpecification.name: outline
toolSpecification.description: Return a compact structural outline (functions/classes/types) of a source file. Supports .py .js .jsx .ts .tsx .go. Use BEFORE editing an unfamiliar file (smaller than fs_read, focused on shape, not content).

toolSpecification.name: browser_console_logs
toolSpecification.description: Read recent browser console messages and uncaught page errors from the sandboxed browser (ring buffer up to 500). Use to debug JS errors after browser_navigate / interactions.

clear.description: Clear the buffer instead of reading.

toolSpecification.name: browser_network
toolSpecification.description: Network monitoring for the sandboxed browser. Actions: start (clear+record), stop, clear, log (default).

filter.description: Substring filter on URL when action=log.

toolSpecification.name: browser_accessibility
toolSpecification.description: Snapshot the accessibility tree of the current page (or a sub-tree by CSS selector via 'root'). Use to inspect interactive structure (roles, names) instead of raw DOM. Cleaner than browser_text for buttons/inputs/links.

interesting_only.description: Default true; false returns full tree.

root.description: Optional CSS selector to scope the snapshot.

toolSpecification.name: browser_emulate
toolSpecification.description: Emulate device / viewport / color scheme / media. Use to test responsive UI, dark mode, print preview. Devices: 'iPhone 14', 'iPhone SE', 'Pixel 7', 'iPad', 'Desktop', 'Desktop 1080p', 'Desktop 4K'.

toolSpecification.name: git
toolSpecification.description: Run a git subcommand in the sandbox. ops: status, diff (cached?, stat?, ref?, path?), log (limit, path?), show (ref), blame (file, line_start?, line_end?), add (files), branch, current_branch, checkout (ref, create_new?), stash (sub?, message?), restore (files, staged?), ls_files (modified?), init.

toolSpecification.name: git_commit
toolSpecification.description: Stage and commit current changes. By default 'git add -A' is run first (set stage=false to skip). Returns the new short hash on success. Use AFTER finishing a logical unit of work. Imperative message referencing the plan step.

toolSpecification.name: run_tests
toolSpecification.description: Detect the test runner (pytest/jest/go) and execute it. Returns a parsed summary 'TESTS=PASS|FAIL ... passed=N failed=N duration=Xs' plus raw tail. Prefer this over execute_bash pytest — the structured header is for follow-up decisions.

toolSpecification.name: lint
toolSpecification.description: Quick syntax/type/style check. .py: ruff if available else py_compile. .js/.jsx/.mjs: node --check. .ts/.tsx: tsc --noEmit if available. Returns 'LINT=OK' or 'LINT=FAIL' plus per-file results.

toolSpecification.name: find_definition
toolSpecification.description: Jump to symbol definition via LSP (pyright for Python, typescript-language-server for TS/JS). Provide `file` plus either (line,character) [0-based] / line_1based, OR `symbol` to auto-locate first occurrence. Returns list of file:line:col definitions.

file.description: File path (absolute or relative to cwd).

symbol.description: Alternative: find first occurrence of this identifier in the file and use its position.

toolSpecification.name: find_references
toolSpecification.description: Find all references to symbol via LSP. Same arg style as find_definition. Optional `include_declaration` (default true). Returns file:line:col list.

file.description: File path (absolute or relative to cwd).

symbol.description: Alternative: find first occurrence of this identifier in the file and use its position.

toolSpecification.name: rename_symbol
toolSpecification.description: Rename a symbol project-wide via LSP. Computes safe edits across files and applies them (with backups). Args: file, new_name, plus position spec (line+character, line_1based, or symbol). Set apply=false for preview.

file.description: File path (absolute or relative to cwd).

symbol.description: Alternative: find first occurrence of this identifier in the file and use its position.

toolSpecification.name: diagnostics
toolSpecification.description: Get type/syntax diagnostics for a file from pyright (.py) or typescript-language-server (.ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx). Args: file, wait_ms (default 4000). Returns clean or list of {severity, location, code, message}.

toolSpecification.name: dev_loop
toolSpecification.description: Self-driving edit-test-fix loop. Implements `task` by editing files (via a subagent with full tool access), then runs the project test suite. On failure, the test output is fed back and the loop iterates up to max_iters (default 5). Returns DEV_LOOP=PASS or DEV_LOOP=FAIL with the last test output.

toolSpecification.name: memory_search
toolSpecification.description: BM25 search over the notebook directory (markdown files, ~/notebook). Use this BEFORE starting a task to find prior decisions, lessons learned, and project context. Cheaper than fs_read-ing many files. Returns top-k chunks with file:line ranges, heading, and snippet.

toolSpecification.name: memory_add
toolSpecification.description: Append a note to the long-term memory (notebook). Default file MEMORY.md; pass `file` (plain filename) to target an existing notebook file. Use this for permanent lessons, decisions, and facts you want future sessions to find.

toolSpecification.name: review_changes
toolSpecification.description: Critic agent: a SECOND LLM reviews a diff for obvious problems (secrets committed, syntax errors, removed tests, dangerous shell ops, disabled security). Returns REVIEW=OK or REVIEW=BLOCK with reasons. If `diff` is not provided, defaults to `git diff HEAD` in the current cwd. Call this BEFORE git_commit on non-trivial changes.

toolSpecification.name: prod_observe
toolSpecification.description: Read-only production observation. ONLY way for you to see the LIVE host (disk-photon) state — your filesystem and shell live inside a sandbox container. Use this when the user asks 'are there errors in the journal?', 'is webchat healthy?', 'how much disk?', 'what was the last commit?', etc. Argument `what` selects the action: 'uptime' (load+memory), 'df' (disk), 'systemctl_status' (with `unit`, default webchat), 'journalctl' (with optional `lines` 1-500 and `grep` substring filter, default 50 lines of webchat), 'git_log' (with `n` 1-50), 'git_diff' (with `ref`, default HEAD~1). Returns JSON {ok, stdout, stderr, returncode, duration_seconds}. No shell, no input interpolation — only whitelisted commands.

toolSpecification.name: gh_pr_open
toolSpecification.description: Open a GitHub Pull Request with files you authored. This is THE only way you can change the deployed code — a human must merge the PR before CD ships it. Branch name MUST start with `kira/` (e.g. `kira/fix-typo`, `kira/feat-x`). Provide title (single line, <72 chars), body (markdown, explain WHAT and WHY), and files (dict mapping repo-relative path → full file content; existing files are overwritten, new files are created). Hard limits: at most 20 files, total <256 KiB, files under `.github/workflows/` are rejected (workflow injection guard). Use this when the user accepts a fix and asks to open a PR — do NOT push directly to main and do NOT bundle unrelated changes. Returns {ok, url, branch, base} or {ok:false, error}.

files.description: map of repo-relative path -> file content

toolSpecification.name: self_status
toolSpecification.description: ALWAYS call this tool when the user asks who you are, what your version is, what git SHA is deployed, what was committed recently, what your coverage is, or any variant of self-introspection. Returns a snapshot: git branch + HEAD + last 5 commits, test count, coverage %, in-flight session count, host name, uptime, sandbox flags, available tool names. Cheap (~5ms), safe, no secrets. Takes no arguments — invoke as `self_status({})`. Do not guess this information from memory; always call the tool.

toolSpecification.name: coverage_status
toolSpecification.description: Read the latest pytest coverage report (coverage.json at repo root) and return overall % plus a list of files sorted by lowest coverage first. Use this when planning what tests to write or which file to refactor with caution. Returns ok=false with hint if no report exists yet — in that case run `make coverage` or `pytest --cov=. --cov-report=json:coverage.json` first. Optional `path` returns line-level detail (missing/excluded lines) for a single file. Optional `limit` truncates the file list (default 20).
